title: International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Amendment Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let regulations confer legal status, privileges and immunities on the International Committee for the Red Cross and the International Criminal Court.
Separate powers would implement Australia’s regional headquarters arrangement with the Red Cross committee and the Court’s privileges agreement, including protection for participating victims.
Privileges would be limited by the relevant agreements, and the new Red Cross provision would avoid extending the law to other organisations with similar characteristics.
changes: Regulations could give the Red Cross committee privileges and legal personality consistent with its Australian headquarters arrangement.
A dedicated regulation power would cover the Court and people identified in its privileges agreement.
The international conference definition would include meetings attended by Australian representatives and representatives of either organisation.
summary.affected: The two organisations, their covered officials and associated people, and victims participating in Court proceedings are affected.

speeches.speaker: Jacinta Collins
speeches.brief: The International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Amendment Bill 2013 was moved to bring the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Criminal Court within the scope of the act, enabling regulations to confer privileges and immunities. The Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013 was proposed to prohibit and invalidate clauses in Commonwealth agreements that restrict not-for-profit entities from advocating on Commonwealth policy issues.

speeches.speaker: Kelvin Thomson
speeches.brief: Moved a bill to bring the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Criminal Court within the International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Act 1963, enabling regulations to confer legal personality and immunities under a 2005 headquarters agreement with the ICRC and paving the way for Australia's accession to the ICC's privileges and immunities agreement.

speeches.speaker: Teresa Gambaro
speeches.brief: Supported the bill extending privileges and immunities to the ICRC and International Criminal Court, noting the ICRC delivered food to 617,000 people and water to 100,000 people in Syria between January and March this year, and recalled the Howard government's 2002 ratification of the Rome Statute following an 18-month inquiry that received more than 250 submissions.
